# LoRa, SF7, 125 kHz

One payload — `sdrflex lora fixture` — transmitted three times. Chirp spread spectrum,
spreading factor 7, 125 kHz bandwidth, coding rate 4/5, sync word 0x12, sampled at
250 kS/s complex on 868.1 MHz.

**Nobody transmitted this.** It is generated by `fixtures/make.mjs`, which for this one
capture shells out to `server/flowgraphs/lora-tx.py` — gr-lora_sdr's own transmitter.

That is the only fixture here not synthesized in JavaScript from a seed, and the reason
is worth stating. A LoRa frame is chirp spread spectrum wrapped in whitening, Hamming
coding, interleaving, a Gray map, a header and a CRC. Writing all of that in JavaScript
to test somebody else's LoRa decoder would mostly be testing *our reimplementation* of
LoRa — and if the reimplementation were wrong in the same way the decoder is, the test
would pass and mean nothing. Using the decoder's own encoder makes the check two-sided
instead: if either half drifts, the other stops agreeing.

Everything ADR-0025 actually asks for still holds. There is no noise and no channel model
in the transmit chain, so regenerating produces a byte-identical file — that was checked,
not assumed. It is 176 kB. And on a machine without GNU Radio, `make.mjs` skips it and
this committed capture stands.

The control is in `web/test/identify.test.mjs`: the same capture decoded at SF9 returns
nothing at all, which is what says the SF7 decode is a decode rather than a decoder
willing to find something anywhere.
